rv.q: Take in the outsized paper blooms rooted in a muddied grass mound from set designer Zoë Hurwitz that is dramatically lit by Daniel Carter-Brennan, and gaze at the empty laddered seat before the story begins.

A lovely exploration of a life and the human experience that struggles to fill the mammoth Soho Theatre Walthamstow The time is finally here: the doors of the long-awaited Soho Theatre Walthamstow are open. And on arrival, the space itself is a spectacle.

You later realise that it may fall victim to the same flaw that the show possesses, in that it implies relatability with the consumer, but doesn’t dismantle the disconnect you have between you and them.
